items.title: Welcome to the NSW Waratahs
items.text:
New South Wales has played representative rugby since 1882, when it first met Queensland. The Waratahs, in sky blue, are the state’s Super Rugby team.

They won Super Rugby in 2014. Sydney’s club competition, the Shute Shield, is where many Waratahs come from.

items.title: From the local club to Super Rugby
items.text:
Every player in the NSW Waratahs squad started at a local club. Talented juniors are picked for representative age-group teams, and the best join the club’s academy.

The academy adds coaching, strength and conditioning, and support with school or work, so players are ready when their chance comes.

data.standfirst: New South Wales has played representative rugby since 1882, when it first met Queensland. The Waratahs, in sky blue, are the state’s Super Rugby team.

image.alt: Sydney Opera House beside the harbour

body.text: They won Super Rugby in 2014. Sydney’s club competition, the Shute Shield, is where many Waratahs come from.
Home games are at Allianz Stadium in Sydney.
1882: New South Wales and Queensland play their first interstate match. 2014: Super Rugby champions. Shute Shield: Sydney’s club competition feeds the Waratahs.

data.headline: Match day at Allianz Stadium: what to know
data.standfirst: Tickets, getting there and what to expect at a home game.

image.alt: A pitch under bright floodlights at night

body.text: Home games at Allianz Stadium are a day out for the whole family. Here is how to plan yours.
Members keep the same seat all season. Single tickets go on sale before each game, and children’s tickets are discounted.
Public transport is the easiest way to Allianz Stadium on game day. Allow extra time: the roads around the ground are busy before kick-off.
Gates open well before kick-off, with activities for kids on the concourse. Stay after the game for signing sessions on selected dates.

data.headline: Inside the academy: from club rugby to Super Rugby
data.standfirst: How young players in New South Wales find their way into the NSW Waratahs squad.

image.alt: A coach talking to players gathered around

body.text: Every player in the NSW Waratahs squad started at a local club. The academy is the bridge between club rugby and the professional game.
Talented juniors are spotted in club and school rugby and in representative age-group teams, then invited to train with the academy.
Coaching, strength and conditioning, and support with school or work, so players are ready when their chance comes.
The same pathway leads to the club’s Super W team.
